name: Off-Highway Motorcycle
description: A two-wheeled motor vehicle the operator straddles, with handlebars, designed for use off a highway whether or not it's also designed for highway use, such as an electric dirt bike like a Sur-Ron or Talaria; one not registered for highways is a limited use off-highway motorcycle. Defined by Wisconsin Statutes §23.335(1)(q), whose OHM program began October 1, 2016.
restrictions: Two wheels, handlebars and a straddle seat, designed for off-highway use; not an electric bicycle, and no limit on motor power or speed

Registered with the DNR for public use, with a decal, to ride off the highways on public OHM trails, areas and routes; private-use registration is optional for riding only on the owner's or family's land
Riders under 12 may not ride it on a roadway, and off the roadway only with a parent, guardian or designated adult 18 or older
Riders 12 and older born after January 1, 1998 need a DNR safety certificate to ride off the highways, except on private land with the owner's consent that isn't open to the public
Riders and passengers under 18 must wear a fastened helmet meeting FMVSS 218, and everyone on an OHM corridor or route must wear glasses, goggles or a face shield
Without highway registration, it may use a roadway only to cross it, cross a bridge or railroad right-of-way, on an unmaintained seasonal road, or on a designated OHM route at the extreme right
Never allowed on an interstate freeway, nor on any other freeway unless the Department of Transportation authorizes it
No operator's license needed to ride a limited use off-highway motorcycle where the OHM law allows it
